memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Jacob continued on his journey and came to the land of the eastern peoples. There he saw a well in the open country, with three flocks of sheep lying near it because the flocks were watered from that well. The stone over the mouth of the well was large. When all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone away from the well's mouth and water the sheep. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well. Jacob asked the shepherds, 'My brothers, where are you from?' 'We're from Harran,' they replied. He said to them, 'Do you know Laban, Nahor's grandson?' 'Yes, we know him,' they answered. Then Jacob asked them, 'Is he well?' 'Yes, he is,' they said, 'and here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.'" - Gen 29:1-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob resumes his long journey and comes at last to the land where his mother's family lives. And where does he arrive? At a well in the open country. Of all the places he might have stopped, he lands exactly where he needs to be — and the very people he is looking for turn out to be right there. "Do you know Laban?" he asks. "Yes... and here comes his daughter Rachel."

There are no coincidences with God. Jacob had left home a lonely fugitive with no map for his future, yet God was quietly guiding every step, leading him straight to his relatives. What looked like a wanderer stumbling upon a random well was, in truth, God arranging a divine appointment. At Bethel, God had promised, "I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go" (Gen 28:15), and here that promise begins to unfold.

We rarely see God's guidance while it is happening. It usually looks like ordinary decisions and chance encounters — a conversation, a wrong turn that becomes a right one, an unexpected meeting. Only later do we look back and realise God was leading us the whole time.

If you feel like you are wandering without a clear path, take heart from Jacob. The God who led him to the right well at the right moment is able to guide your steps too (Prov 3:6). Keep walking in trust; He is directing your journey more than you know.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I later realised God was guiding me all along?
2. Do I trust God to direct my steps even when the path is unclear?
3. Am I watching for the "divine appointments" in my ordinary days?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You guide my steps even when I feel like I am wandering. Help me to trust Your leading and to notice the appointments You arrange along my way. Amen.
